Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 7425e8167507fe512d8ac0825acda4aebf0a7ca0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Oct 2021 15:40:05 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] drm/msm: unlock on error in get_sched_entity()

Add a missing unlock on the error path if drm_sched_entity_init() fails.

Fixes: 68002469e571 ("drm/msm: One sched entity per process per priority")
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20211011124005.GE15188@kili
Signed-off-by: Rob Clark <robdclark@chromium.org>

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/msm_submitqueue.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/msm_submitqueue.c
index b8621c6e0554..7cb158bcbcf6 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/msm_submitqueue.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/msm/msm_submitqueue.c
@@ -101,6 +101,7 @@ get_sched_entity(struct msm_file_private *ctx, struct msm_ringbuffer *ring,
 
 		ret = drm_sched_entity_init(entity, sched_prio, &sched, 1, NULL);
 		if (ret) {
+			mutex_unlock(&entity_lock);
 			kfree(entity);
 			return ERR_PTR(ret);
 		}
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/gpu/drm/msm/msm_submitqueue.c`**
- A line was added to unlock a mutex (`mutex_unlock(&entity_lock);`) in the error handling path of the `get_sched_entity` function. This occurs if the call to `drm_sched_entity_init(entity, sched_prio, &sched, 1, NULL)` fails, ensuring that the mutex is properly released before returning an error pointer.

### Relationships
The modification addresses a bug related to resource management in the `get_sched_entity` function. Specifically, it ensures that if the initialization of the scheduling entity fails, the previously acquired lock is released, preventing potential deadlocks or resource contention issues. This change is a direct fix to the issue introduced in a prior commit (identified by the hash `68002469e571`), which established the scheduling entity per process per priority. The addition of the unlock operation enhances the robustness of the error handling in the function.
